Semester 1: Foundations of Nursing

Read the summary line. If it feels unfamiliar, open the chapter and study the diagram.

Applied Anatomy

Introduction to Anatomical Terms & Body Organisation

  • The language of anatomy — positions, planes, movement terms and how the body is organised from cell to system.
  • Use correct anatomical terms for position and movement
  • Name the planes and body cavities

Applied Physiology

General Physiology & Cell Physiology

  • How cells build themselves, move substances across membranes and hold the internal environment steady — the foundation of all nursing science.
  • Entry level
  • Intermediate level

Applied Psychology

Introduction to Psychology

  • What psychology is, its goals and branches, and why it matters for nursing care.
  • Define psychology and state its goals
  • List the main branches of psychology

Applied Sociology

Introduction to Sociology

  • What sociology is, its scope and why society shapes health and nursing care.
  • Define sociology and state its scope
  • Explain the difference between sociology and psychology

Communicative English

What is Communication?

  • What communication is, its process, types and why it matters in nursing.
  • Define communication and list its elements
  • Describe the communication process

Nursing Foundation I

Health & Illness

  • Concepts of health and illness, the health–illness continuum, Maslow’s needs and factors affecting health.
  • Define health and illness
  • Describe the health–illness continuum

Applied Anatomy

Respiratory System

  • The organs that bring air in and out, and the tiny air sacs where oxygen enters the blood.
  • Name the organs of the respiratory tract in the correct order
  • Describe the lungs, pleura and diaphragm

Applied Physiology

Respiratory System

  • How the lungs move air, exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide, and keep blood gases within the narrow range the body can tolerate.
  • Entry level
  • Intermediate level

Applied Psychology

Biological Basis of Behaviour

  • The neuron, nervous system, brain structures and endocrine influence on behaviour.
  • Describe the parts of a neuron and how a nerve impulse travels
  • Name the main parts of the brain and their functions

Applied Sociology

Social Structure

  • Social structure, status and role, groups, institutions and how they influence health behaviour.
  • Define social structure, status and role
  • Describe primary and secondary groups

Communicative English

Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing & Grammar

  • The four language skills LSRW and basic grammar for professional English.
  • Explain the four language skills LSRW
  • Describe basic grammar points for nursing English

Nursing Foundation I

Health Care Delivery Systems

  • India's health care delivery system — PHC, CHC, district hospital, Ayushman Bharat and levels of care.
  • Describe levels of health care in India
  • Explain the PHC and CHC system

Applied Anatomy

Digestive System

  • The mouth-to-anus tube and its helper organs, and how food is broken down and absorbed.
  • Name the organs of the digestive tract in order
  • Describe the structure and function of the stomach and small intestine

Applied Physiology

Digestive System

  • How food is digested and absorbed — enzymes, bile, peristalsis and the liver's metabolic role.
  • List the digestive enzymes and what each breaks down
  • Explain the roles of bile and peristalsis

Applied Psychology

Mental Health & Mental Hygiene

  • What mental health means, signs of good and poor mental health, and how to promote it.
  • Define mental health and mental illness
  • List characteristics of a mentally healthy person

Applied Sociology

Culture

  • Culture, its components, cultural diversity and cultural competence in nursing care.
  • Define culture and list its components
  • Explain cultural relativism and ethnocentrism

Communicative English

Attentive Listening

  • What attentive listening is, its types, barriers and how to listen well to patients.
  • Define attentive listening
  • List types of listening

Nursing Foundation I

History of Nursing & Nursing as a Profession

  • Nursing history, Florence Nightingale, nursing in India, INC and nursing as a profession.
  • Describe Florence Nightingale’s contribution
  • Outline the history of nursing in India

Applied Anatomy

Circulatory & Lymphatic System

  • The heart, blood vessels and lymphatics — how blood is pumped, where it travels and how tissue fluid is drained.
  • Describe the four chambers and four valves of the heart
  • Trace the pulmonary and systemic circulation

Applied Physiology

Circulatory & Lymphatic System

  • How the heart pumps blood, the cardiac cycle, blood pressure regulation and lymphatic return.
  • Describe the cardiac cycle and heart sounds
  • Define cardiac output and stroke volume

Applied Psychology

Developmental Psychology

  • Human development across the lifespan — Erikson's stages, Piaget's stages and nursing implications.
  • Describe Erikson's stages of psychosocial development
  • Outline Piaget's stages of cognitive development

Applied Sociology

Family & Marriage

  • Types of family and marriage, family functions and the family’s role in health and illness.
  • Define family and list its types
  • Describe types of marriage

Communicative English

Speaking & Effective Conversation

  • Speaking clearly, tone, pronunciation, and effective patient conversation.
  • Describe features of clear speaking
  • Explain tone and pronunciation in patient talk

Nursing Foundation I

Communication & Nurse–Patient Relationship

  • Nurse–patient communication, therapeutic relationship, phases and barriers.
  • Describe the nurse–patient relationship
  • List phases of the relationship

Applied Anatomy

Endocrine System

  • The ductless glands, the hormones they release and the body functions they control.
  • Name the major endocrine glands and their positions
  • State the main hormone of each gland and its action

Applied Physiology

Blood

  • Blood composition, plasma, red and white cells, platelets, blood groups and clotting.
  • List the components of blood and their functions
  • Describe the ABO and Rh blood group systems

Applied Psychology

Personality

  • What personality is, major theories (Freud, trait, humanistic) and how personality affects health behaviour.
  • Define personality
  • Describe Freud's id, ego and superego

Applied Sociology

Social Stratification

  • Social stratification — caste, class, gender and inequality — and how they affect access to health care.
  • Define social stratification
  • Describe caste and class in India

Communicative English

Reading Skills

  • Reading skills for nurses — skimming, scanning, SQ3R and reading charts and labels.
  • Describe skimming and scanning
  • Explain the SQ3R method

Nursing Foundation I

Documentation & Reporting

  • Nursing records, reporting, legal rules and methods such as SOAP and narrative.
  • State the purposes of nursing records
  • Describe methods of documentation

Applied Anatomy

Sensory Organs

  • The eye, ear, nose, tongue and skin — how the body receives light, sound, smell, taste and touch.
  • Name the three layers of the eye and the parts of the ear
  • Explain how light and sound are converted into nerve impulses

Applied Physiology

Endocrine System

  • How endocrine glands regulate metabolism, growth, stress and reproduction through hormones and feedback.
  • Name the main hormones of the pituitary, thyroid and adrenal glands
  • Explain negative feedback control of hormone secretion

Applied Psychology

Cognitive Processes

  • Sensation, perception, attention, memory, learning, thinking and intelligence.
  • Describe the stages of memory (sensory, short-term, long-term)
  • Explain classical and operant conditioning

Applied Sociology

Social Organisation & Disorganisation

  • Social organisation, social control, and social disorganisation such as crime and family breakdown.
  • Define social organisation and social disorganisation
  • Describe agents of social control

Communicative English

Writing Skills

  • Writing clear nursing notes, reports and records — SOAP, accuracy and legal rules.
  • Write a clear nursing note
  • Use the SOAP method

Nursing Foundation I

Vital Signs

  • Temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and oxygen saturation — normal values, how to measure them and when to report.
  • State the normal range of temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and SpO₂
  • Identify the sites used to measure each vital sign

Applied Anatomy

Musculoskeletal System

  • Bones, joints and muscles — the skeleton's framework, types of joints and how skeletal muscle moves the body.
  • Classify bones by shape and name the parts of a long bone
  • Name the types of synovial joints with examples

Applied Physiology

Special Senses

  • How the eye sees, the ear hears and balances, and the nose and tongue detect smell and taste.
  • Explain how the eye focuses light on the retina
  • Describe how sound becomes a nerve impulse

Applied Psychology

Motivation & Emotional Processes

  • Motivation theories, emotions, stress and coping — how they affect patient behaviour and recovery.
  • Describe Maslow's hierarchy of needs
  • Define emotion and list basic emotions

Applied Sociology

Clinical Sociology

  • Applying sociology in health care — the patient as a social person, the hospital as a social system, and the sick role.
  • Define clinical sociology
  • Describe the patient as a social person

Communicative English

Integrated LSRW Skills

  • Using listening, speaking, reading and writing together in real nursing situations.
  • Explain how LSRW skills work together
  • Give an example of integrated skills in patient education

Nursing Foundation I

Equipment & Linen

  • Hospital equipment, linen, care and handling, and the nurse's responsibility.
  • List common hospital equipment and linen
  • Describe care and handling of equipment and linen

Applied Anatomy

Renal System

  • The kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra — how urine is formed and how the body controls water and salt balance.
  • Trace the urinary tract from kidney to urethra
  • Describe the structure of a nephron and how urine forms

Applied Physiology

Musculoskeletal System

  • How bone grows and repairs, how muscle contracts, and how joints move the body.
  • Describe bone growth and fracture repair
  • Explain how skeletal muscle contracts

Applied Psychology

Psychological Assessment & Tests

  • How psychological assessment is done — interviews, observation, tests and what nurses should know.
  • List methods of psychological assessment
  • Describe what IQ and personality tests measure

Nursing Foundation I

Infection Control & Asepsis

  • Chain of infection, hand hygiene, PPE, standard precautions and aseptic technique.
  • Describe the chain of infection
  • Demonstrate correct hand hygiene

Applied Anatomy

Reproductive System

  • Male and female reproductive organs, gametes, fertilisation, the menstrual cycle and pregnancy support.
  • Name the male and female reproductive organs
  • Describe the menstrual cycle and ovulation

Applied Physiology

Renal System

  • How the kidneys form urine, control water, salt, acid–base balance and blood pressure.
  • Describe glomerular filtration, reabsorption and secretion
  • State normal urine output and specific gravity

Applied Psychology

Application of Soft Skills

  • Soft skills for nurses — communication, teamwork, empathy, time management and professional behaviour.
  • List key soft skills for nursing
  • Describe empathy and active listening

Nursing Foundation I

Comfort, Rest, Sleep & Pain

  • Comfort measures, rest and sleep, pain types and assessment, and non-drug pain relief.
  • Describe comfort measures and positions
  • Explain factors affecting sleep and how to promote it

Applied Anatomy

Nervous System

  • The brain, spinal cord and nerves — central and peripheral nervous system and their main functions.
  • Name the main parts of the brain and their functions
  • Describe the spinal cord and its protective coverings

Applied Physiology

Reproductive System & Nervous System

  • Hormonal control of reproduction and how the nervous system senses, integrates and responds.
  • Describe the menstrual cycle hormones and phases
  • Explain how a nerve impulse travels along a neuron

Applied Psychology

Self-Empowerment

  • Self-awareness, self-esteem, assertiveness and stress management for personal and professional growth.
  • Define self-awareness, self-esteem and assertiveness
  • Describe assertive, aggressive and passive communication

Nursing Foundation I

Promoting Safety in Health Care + First Aid

  • Patient safety, fall prevention, fire safety and first aid for common emergencies.
  • Describe patient safety and fall prevention
  • Explain fire safety in a hospital
